quests.instruction: Write the capital letter C: a big curve that opens to the right.
quests.question: C
quests.hint: Start near the top right, curve left and down around the middle, and stop near the bottom right. Do not close it.
quests.explanation: C is an open curve that travels counter-clockwise. Leaving the right side open is what makes it different from O.
quests.funFact: In Roman numerals the letter C stands for 100, from the Latin word 'centum'.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letter O: a full circle that closes neatly at the top.
quests.question: O
quests.hint: Start at the top and go to the left, down, around the bottom and up, meeting where you began.
quests.explanation: O uses the same counter-clockwise path as C, but you carry on until the circle closes. A neat closure shows control.
quests.funFact: In English, the letter O has many sounds, as in 'go', 'dog', 'to' and 'one'.

quests.instruction: Write C and O side by side. Make them the same height and width.
quests.question: C O
quests.hint: Think of O as a closed C. Check that both reach the top line and the bottom line.
quests.explanation: Matching two round letters means matching width as well as height. C should be as wide as O, even though one side is open.
quests.funFact: Type designers make round letters like C and O a tiny bit taller than flat letters, since curves look smaller than lines of the same height.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letter G: start like C, then add a short bar going inward in the middle.
quests.question: G
quests.hint: Draw a C. When you reach the bottom right, curve up a little, then add a short line going left in the middle.
quests.explanation: G is C with a small shelf. The shelf closes the opening halfway so G does not look like a plain C.
quests.funFact: The Romans made the letter G by adding a small bar to the letter C.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letter Q: draw an O, then add a small tail at the bottom right.
quests.question: Q
quests.hint: Make a closed circle first. Then lift your pen and draw a short slant crossing the bottom right of the circle.
quests.explanation: Q is an O with a tail. The tail is added last, and it should be small so the circle stays the main part.
quests.funFact: In English words, the letter Q is almost always followed by the letter U, as in 'queen'.

quests.instruction: Write G and Q next to each other. Make the shelf and the tail clear.
quests.question: G Q
quests.hint: G has a shelf inside, so make it point left. Q has a tail on the outside, so make it point down-right.
quests.explanation: Both letters are almost round, so the small extra part has to be clear. Checking the extra part is how you tell them apart.
quests.funFact: The word 'quiz' contains Q and Z, two of the rarest letters in English.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letter S: a curve at the top, a curve at the bottom, and a smooth turn in the middle.
quests.question: S
quests.hint: Start at the top right and curve to the left, sweep through the middle to the right, then curve down and finish at the bottom left.
quests.explanation: S changes curve direction in the middle. Going slowly through that turn keeps the two curves balanced instead of making a zigzag.
quests.funFact: S is the most common first letter of English words.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letter U: down one side, a round curve at the bottom, and up the other side.
quests.question: U
quests.hint: Pull down on the left, curve smoothly through the bottom, and go back up on the right. Both sides should reach the top line.
quests.explanation: U is a cup arc with two upright sides. A round bottom, not a pointy one, is what separates U from V.
quests.funFact: The name of the letter U sounds exactly like the word 'you'.

quests.instruction: Write S and U next to each other. Check that both reach the top and the bottom line.
quests.question: S U
quests.hint: S is curvy in the middle, and U is straight on the sides. Keep both between the same two lines.
quests.explanation: Letters with different shapes still need the same height. Checking top and bottom lines each time keeps writing tidy.
quests.funFact: A U-turn in a road is named for its shape, since the road makes a U.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letter J: a line going down that hooks to the left at the bottom.
quests.question: J
quests.hint: Pull straight down, and just before the baseline curve to the left like a fishhook.
quests.explanation: J has a straight stem and a hook. The hook turns left so the letter reads as a J and not as a backwards one.
quests.funFact: J is one of the last letters added to the English alphabet.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letter D: a standing line and a big curve on its right side.
quests.question: D
quests.hint: Pull down first. Go back to the top and draw a large curve that swings to the right and joins the bottom of the line.
quests.explanation: D is a stem plus half of a circle. The curve starts exactly at the top of the stem and meets exactly at the bottom.
quests.funFact: D began as the Phoenician letter 'daleth', which means door.

quests.instruction: Write J and D together. Decide which letter has a hook and which has a belly.
quests.question: J D
quests.hint: J gets a hook at the bottom. D gets a big round belly on the right. Check the heights match.
quests.explanation: Comparing a hook and a belly helps you notice that even letters that look different use stems and curves.
quests.funFact: In Roman numerals, D stands for 500.

quests.instruction: From memory, write the round letters C, O and G in a row.
quests.question: C O G
quests.hint: All three start at the top right or top and go counter-clockwise. Add the shelf to G last.
quests.explanation: Round letters share the same starting point and direction. Remembering the path helps you recall all three at once.
quests.funFact: Typefaces such as Times New Roman and Arial are called fonts, and there are many thousands of them.

quests.instruction: Write U and S from memory. One is round and curvy, one is smooth and straight on both sides.
quests.question: U S
quests.hint: Write U with a smooth bottom and two vertical sides. Then S with a curve at top and bottom.
quests.explanation: Describing letters by their parts, such as 'sides and bottom', lets you rebuild them without looking.
quests.funFact: Sign languages have a handshape for every letter, which is called fingerspelling.

quests.instruction: Write D, J and Q in a row. Make each part clear.
quests.question: D J Q
quests.hint: D has a belly, J has a hook, and Q has a tail. Say the extra part aloud before you write it.
quests.explanation: Mixed-letter practice is harder than copying one letter, because you have to decide each shape each time.
quests.funFact: Spelling bees are contests where children spell words aloud, letter by letter.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letter P: a standing line with a bump at the top right.
quests.question: P
quests.hint: Pull down first. Go back to the top and draw a bump that swings right and returns to the middle of the stem.
quests.explanation: P is a stem plus a small round bowl in the top half. The bowl should end halfway down the stem.
quests.funFact: P began from a Phoenician letter called 'pe', which means mouth.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letter R: write a P, then add a leg that kicks out to the right.
quests.question: R
quests.hint: Make a P first. From where the bump meets the stem, slant down and out to the baseline.
quests.explanation: R is a P with a leg. The leg starts from the bowl's end and finishes at the baseline.
quests.funFact: The Phoenician letter 'resh', which became R, meant head.

quests.instruction: Write P and R together. Check the bump on both is the same size.
quests.question: P R
quests.hint: Write the bump of P first, then repeat the exact same bump for R. Add the leg last.
quests.explanation: Reusing the same bowl in both letters keeps them tidy. Only the leg is new.
quests.funFact: A consonant is a sound made by blocking or narrowing the air with your lips, teeth or tongue.

quests.instruction: Write the capital letter B: a standing line with two bumps on its right.
quests.question: B
quests.hint: Pull down first. Draw the top bump from the top back to the middle, then a slightly bigger bump from the middle to the bottom.
quests.explanation: B is a stem with two bowls, and the lower one is a little bigger. Both bumps must touch the stem in the middle.
quests.funFact: B comes from the Phoenician letter 'beth', which means house.

quests.instruction: Write B, P and R in a row. Count the bumps in each one.
quests.question: B P R
quests.hint: B has two bumps, P has one, and R has one and a leg. Say 'two, one, one' as you go.
quests.explanation: Counting the bumps lets you tell similar letters apart quickly. This is how readers recognize letters, too.
quests.funFact: Typographers call the round parts of letters 'bowls'.

quests.instruction: Write B and D next to each other. Their bumps are different.
quests.question: B D
quests.hint: B has two bumps and D has one big curve. Start both with a line going down.
quests.explanation: B and D are often confused. Remember that D has a single belly and B has two.
quests.funFact: Mixing up similar letters is very common when learning to write, and it fades with practice.

quests.instruction: Write P, B and D, all stem letters with bumps, in a row.
quests.question: P B D
quests.hint: Draw each stem first, top to bottom, then add the bump or bumps on the right. Keep all three the same height.
quests.explanation: Stem-and-bump letters share a start. Only the bumps differ, so you should plan them before drawing.
quests.funFact: The ABC song has the same tune as 'Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star'.

quests.instruction: Write R and K. Both have a leg or slant that kicks out to the right.
quests.question: R K
quests.hint: R has a bump on top and a leg below. K has two slants meeting the stem. Take care where each leg begins.
quests.explanation: Both letters have a stem and an outgoing leg, so the first part of the work is the same. The difference is the bump.
quests.funFact: Computer keyboards show capital letters on their keys, even though pressing them usually types lowercase.

quests.instruction: Write U and V together. One has a round bottom, one a pointed bottom.
quests.question: U V
quests.hint: For U, curve the bottom smoothly. For V, stop at a sharp point before you go up.
quests.explanation: A round bottom and a pointed bottom are very different strokes. Telling them apart in your hand helps your handwriting stay clear.
quests.funFact: The first practical typewriters were sold in the 1870s.

quests.instruction: Write the first three letters of the alphabet in order, with space between them.
quests.question: A B C
quests.hint: Say 'A, B, C' as you write. Leave a gap about as wide as a finger between letters.
quests.explanation: Writing in alphabet order builds a clear sense of sequence. Every letter should be the same height.
quests.funFact: Children in many countries learn the alphabet by singing it.

quests.instruction: Now write the next three letters, D, E and F, with equal gaps.
quests.question: D E F
quests.hint: Start each letter at the top line. Check that D's curve and E's bars all stay on the lines.
quests.explanation: Writing sets of letters in a row builds stamina. Equal gaps show control.
quests.funFact: The Hawaiian alphabet has only 13 letters, including its five vowels.

quests.instruction: Write the first six letters of the alphabet in a row.
quests.question: A B C D E F
quests.correctAnswer: A B C D E F
quests.hint: Plan the width of the line first so all six fit. Keep the gaps equal and the heights the same.
quests.explanation: Planning space for six letters is a big step toward writing words. Check that none are crowded.
quests.funFact: The English alphabet comes from the Latin alphabet, which the Romans spread across Europe.

quests.instruction: Write G, H and I in a row. Start each at the top line.
quests.question: G H I
quests.hint: G begins with a curve, H and I begin with a straight stem. Keep all three the same height.
quests.explanation: Switching between curved and straight starts makes your hand flexible.
quests.funFact: The Rotokas alphabet, used in Papua New Guinea, has only 12 letters.

quests.instruction: Write J, K, L and M in a row. Watch your spacing.
quests.question: J K L M
quests.hint: Four letters need careful planning. J has a hook, K has slants, L has a corner and M has a zigzag.
quests.explanation: Four different shapes in a row make you switch strokes quickly and keep the spacing even.
quests.funFact: The Greek alphabet has 24 letters, while English has 26.

quests.instruction: Write G through M in order, keeping equal gaps.
quests.question: G H I J K L M
quests.correctAnswer: G H I J K L M
quests.hint: Say the letters as you write them. If the row is getting full, make the letters a little narrower, not taller.
quests.explanation: Seven letters is a long row. Keeping size and gaps even, from the first to the last, shows true control.
quests.funFact: Capital letters were once the only letters in the Roman alphabet; lowercase forms came later.
